items.title: Canva Craft
items.summary: Turn prompts into design-ready images you can edit
items.body: Canva Craft is Canva’s first in-house image model, built for marketers, creators and designers who need images that work as designs, not just pictures. Unlike models trained mostly on photos that render pixels straight from a prompt, Craft learned from millions of Canva templates and plans the composition first, then renders it at 2K in 30+ aspect ratios. Expect legible text in 55 languages, precise placement and outputs you can split into editable layers. Live in Canva today, plus API.

In Slack, the CSV is attached in the message's thread; emails and the automation's run history get a Download CSV link. Downloads go through Basedash, so recipients need access to the automation to open them. Ask for it once. Get the CSV every week.

items.body:
Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro

Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026".

They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same).

The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.

Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others.

items.body: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression.
